title: Exemplars in Disguise: Pure Exemplar Models Mimic Abstraction-First Learning
abstract: arXiv:2608.00821v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Whether idiosyncratic, item-specific knowledge is learned before abstract class-level generalizations, or vice versa, is a central question in language learning, with exemplar and abstraction-based theories making opposite predictions. Recent methods have claimed to show that, at least for large language models, abstract knowledge is learned first. We show that these methods fall short: pure memorizer models with no abstract representations can appear, by the same criteria, to learn either item-specific or class-level knowledge first, depending on their sensitivity to individual observations, with the transition point governed by the distributional properties of the input. We further argue that the distinction between item-specific and abstract knowledge may be ill-defined for distributed representations, as a word's class-level properties may not be separable from its item-specific properties.

translated_title: 伪装中的范例：纯范例模型模仿抽象优先学习
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.00821v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：在语言学习中，是先学习特殊的、项目特定的知识，还是先学习抽象的类别级概括，这是一个核心问题，范例理论和基于抽象的理论对此做出了相反的预测。最近的研究声称表明，至少对于大型语言模型而言，抽象知识是首先被学习的。我们证明这些方法存在缺陷：纯记忆模型（没有抽象表示）根据相同标准，可能看起来是先学习项目特定知识或类别级知识，这取决于它们对单个观测的敏感性，其转折点由输入的分布特性决定。我们进一步论证，对于分布式表示而言，项目特定知识与抽象知识之间的区分可能是不明确的，因为一个词的类别级属性可能无法与其项目特定属性分离。
tldr: 本文揭示了纯记忆模型在特定条件下会伪装成抽象优先学习，挑战了大型语言模型先学抽象知识的论断，并指出分布式表示中项目特定与抽象知识的区分可能不成立。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that pure memorizer models can mimic abstraction-first learning under certain conditions, challenging claims that large language models learn abstract knowledge first, and argues the distinction between item-specific and abstract knowledge may be ill-defined for distributed representations.
